### Observed differences

- **A08 became concentrated on a single resource.** In the earlier window, A08 executions were spread across about 17 different resources, with the busiest handling about 18 in 100 executions (concentration index about 0.11); in the later window, every observed A08 execution went to one resource, User_121 (top share 100 in 100, concentration 1.0). The profiles rest on 108 traces before and 120 after. [ASSIGN003, CONC001]

- **Several activities shifted between groups of resources.** For A01, A03, A13, A14, A17 and A21, resources that each held roughly 4–12 in 100 of the executions in the earlier window (including User_49, with about 7–12 in 100 on each of them) lost most or all of that share in the later window, while a largely different group — including User_56, rising from none to about 6–11 in 100 — took over at similar per-resource shares. The share handled by resources outside the leading groups also grew slightly (A01: about 38 → 45 in 100; A21: about 30 → 35 in 100). Each profile rests on roughly 120–275 observations per window. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007]

- **Longer gaps between A04 and A01 completions in the upper tail.** The elapsed time from an A04 completion to the next A01 completion kept a nearly unchanged median (about 24 vs 25 hours), but its 75th percentile rose from about 31 to about 71 hours and its mean from about 26.5 to about 44 hours (200 observations in each window); the difference is larger than in all but about 1 of 2000 random re-splits. [TWAIT001]

- **A negligible timing difference.** Consecutive A20 → A10 completion pairs appeared in 7 of 200 traces before and 17 of 200 after, but the gaps are well under a second in both windows (means about 0.09 vs 0.06 seconds). [TWAIT002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a resource reallocation. In the earlier window, A08 was handled jointly by about 17 resources, whereas in the later window the single resource User_121 carried all observed A08 executions; over the same period, A01, A03, A13, A14, A17 and A21 moved from one group of regularly used resources (including User_49) to a largely different group (including User_56), with somewhat more of the work spread over minor resources. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN003, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007, CONC001]

The resource family produced 8 qualifying items against roughly 0.005 expected if nothing had changed — far beyond what an unchanged process typically yields — all six reassignment profiles shift in the same direction (one consistent pattern rather than six independent findings), and the A08 concentration is shown directly by two indicators on 108–120 traces each. No control-flow item qualified (0 against about 0.16 expected), so no structural difference was detected. Limitation: the resource codes are anonymous, and because so many activities shifted together, the evidence cannot separate a reassignment of these specific activities from a pool-wide change in which resources were available. [ASSIGN001, ASSIGN002, ASSIGN003, ASSIGN004, ASSIGN005, ASSIGN006, ASSIGN007, CONC001]

Other differences:
- A timing change: the gap from A04 completion to the next A01 completion lengthened in its upper tail (75th percentile about 31 → 71 hours; mean about 26.5 → 44 hours; median nearly unchanged), and the time family produced 2 items against about 0.017 expected without a change. The indicator measures elapsed time between consecutive completions, so the evidence cannot show where the extra time arises, nor rule out a link to the resource reallocation. [TWAIT001]
- A minor difference: consecutive A20 → A10 pairs occurred in 7 versus 17 traces with gaps under a second in both windows — practically negligible and based on few observations. [TWAIT002]
